story.lore.l13.title: The Room Above the Workshop
story.lore.l13.body:
The roof leaks over the basin, not over the bed. I have not fixed it because the basin tells me when the upper channel starts backing up. You may move the basin when you move in. Do not move the bed beneath the leak.

There is a second key. It is yours even when you disagree with the people downstairs.

If you leave the sanctuary one day, leave a note about which stones slip in rain. That will be more useful than a poem about our kindness.

— Lan
story.lore.l13.inspect: Read The Room Above the Workshop
story.lore.l14.title: An Allocation Reply
story.lore.l14.body:
We can measure the east branch every third morning. We cannot promise a reader every night; our only bridge hand also looks after the mill.

If the sanctuary needs a night check, put its own name in that box. Please do not use "the community" where you mean whichever neighbour is too embarrassed to refuse.

We will hear a revised schedule. The lower steps can serve as a meeting place after the water is tested.

The reply carries three different thumb marks. None touches the empty night column.
story.lore.l15.title: Ash Rather Than Ink
story.lore.l15.body:
Do not sweep this wall until the names have been copied.

The workers left marks for the rooms they had checked. A long stroke means empty. A circle means someone still needs help reaching the stair. No mark means nobody has looked.

The office counted unmarked rooms as empty. We did not.

I am leaving the lamp at the circle nearest the channel. The light will not hold back water, but a person will know where to begin.

The last line is pressed in the ash by the heel of a hand rather than written with a brush.
story.lore.l16.title: A Training Weight
story.lore.l16.body:
The iron sleeve adds weight to the practice sword. Remove it when the wrist shakes.

A heavier sword does not prove a stronger foundation. Sometimes it only proves that a person is afraid to be seen putting it down.

After a break, return to the first cut. Check the feet. Breathe before the blade moves. If your shoulder hurts tomorrow, tell someone before training again.

The sleeve is polished where many hands have taken it off. Its hook is lower than the hook for the sword.
story.lore.l17.title: Festival Cloth Invoice
story.lore.l17.body:
Six lengths of blue cloth, two of yellow. No red left; use the yellow for the river gate and tell the children it was the plan all along.

Repair the old frames before ordering more. The lanterns do not need to be identical. Visitors will find their houses faster if they recognize their own crooked one.

Mei asked for extra wick for the spillway lamp. Add it without charging the festival account. That lamp is for work.

At the bottom, someone has drawn a lantern with four unequal corners and written: Our house.
story.lore.l18.title: A Request Without a Seal
story.lore.l18.body:
When the binding is opened, do not keep a copy of me because it might be useful.

You may retain the valve readings and my written maintenance requests. They belong to the work. You may tell people my name and what the thirty days became. You do not need a living answer from me to prove that it happened.

I would like one quiet moment without the alarm. After that, let the pattern go.

— Shen Heng

Lan has copied the words exactly and left the box marked Consent empty; this page is a request, not permission to use his mind.
story.lore.l18.inspect: Read A Request Without a Seal
